answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the ferrous checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The basalt graph is rebuilt each epoch, thus the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the sonnet audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 3 times its size, so a group of 78 keys loses far more than 78 single identities would. That is 4 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
